newsitem.title: CANADA: U.S. researcher demands Senate action on Busang.
newsitem.headline: U.S. researcher demands Senate action on Busang.

text.p: The director of research for a U.S. brokerage has asked for a U.S. Senate hearing on the battle for control of the rich Busang gold discovery in Indonesia.
Andrew Racz of Bishop, Rosen and Co Inc said on Friday he sent a letter dated January 23 to Alfonse D'Amato, chairman of the Senate banking committee, officially requesting a hearing.

Racz complained that the Indonesian government had not allowed Bre-X Minerals Ltd, which discovered the huge Busang deposit, to use an open bidding process to find a major mining company to act as its partner in Busang.
"If the Senate overlooks the current games in Jakarta, we are giving American blessings to the most un-American values," Racz said in his letter.

In November, the Indonesian government told Bre-X to form a joint venture with Toronto-based Barrick Gold Corp, with Bre-X keeping 22.5 percent of its stake, Barrick getting 67.5 percent and the government 10 percent.
The companies are still negotiating. Vancouver-based Placer Dome Inc has also said it wants to bid on Busang.
All three companies are listed in Toronto as well as on U.S. exchanges.
